_comment: THE GAP (counterplay diagnostic, 2026-07-02 ledger), env-gated SWEG_TARGET_ECONOMICS, default OFF. This is an ARTIFICIAL-INTELLIGENCE PILOTING HEURISTIC, NOT a Warhammer 40,000 10th-edition game rule — there is no codex or core rule that tells a player which target to shoot. Following the precedent of simulator.focus_fire and simulator.am_advance_discipline (both explicitly-flagged AI design heuristics), this entry quotes the core wound-roll-and-save wording the heuristic's expected-unsaved-damage math is built from, and cites the real-world target-priority doctrine that motivates it: commit small arms into a target they can actually kill (a low-Wounds War Dog) rather than dumping fire into a hull the weapon cannot wound at all (a Toughness-12, 2+ save Knight). Measured before the fix: roughly 35 consecutive zero-damage shooting activations into Knight hulls per the diagnostic trace, 72.8 percent of shots into Knights dealing zero damage, while 2-victory-point War Dogs the same guns could kill sat on objective markers untouched. The mechanic does not change combat math or draw any new random number — it only re-points the existing shooting picker's `min()` choice among already-legal in-range, in-line-of-sight candidates toward the ones this attacker's weapon can meaningfully hurt.

simulator.target_economics.rule_name: Wound roll (Strength vs Toughness) + Saving throw / invulnerable save (10e Core Rules, Shooting phase) — ranged target-priority piloting heuristic
simulator.target_economics.quoted_text: If the Strength characteristic of the weapon used is equal to the Toughness characteristic of the target model's unit, a Wound roll of 4+ is required... After all of the attacks a unit is making have been resolved, for each of those attacks that successfully wounded the target unit, the player commanding that unit can attempt a saving throw... if that unit has an invulnerable save, the player can use that instead of their normal saving throw.
simulator.target_economics.trigger: SWEG_TARGET_ECONOMICS=1 (default off, byte-identical when unset). For every enemy unit in the acting model's LoS-and-range candidate pool during the Shooting phase, compute the attacker's expected unsaved damage against that candidate this activation (shots, hit fraction, Strength-vs-Toughness wound fraction raised to any matching Anti-X floor, the fraction of wounds that get through the target's armour or invulnerable save, and damage per shot — reusing simulator._ranged_expected_wounds, the same expected-damage math the wave-101 collective focus-fire gate already uses), expressed as a fraction of the candidate's own current health.
simulator.target_economics.effect: AI shooting target-selection heuristic. A candidate this attacker's weapon cannot meaningfully wound at all (expected unsaved damage is 0.0, e.g. a Strength-3 lasgun against a Toughness-12 2+ save Knight) is strongly deprioritised (the target-priority bonus floors at 0.35x, dividing the picker's lowest-current-health score up rather than down). A candidate this attacker's weapon can outright remove this activation (expected unsaved damage saturates at or above the candidate's current health) is strongly prioritised (the bonus caps at 2.0x, matching the top of the range the loop has already adopted for other class biases such as Astartes Oath of Moment). This is an AI design heuristic, not a 10e rule — the quoted core wound-roll and saving-throw wording is the combat math the heuristic's expected-damage figure is built from; it does not alter any dice, roll, or damage value, it only changes which already-legal target the AI's shooting picker selects. Faithful and even-handed: it fires for ALL factions against ANY in-range, in-line-of-sight candidate, and it composes multiplicatively with the existing screen / synapse / transport / Astartes-Oath / Votann / Chaos-Knights-dread-cascade / Drukhari-fragile-flyer / kite / threat-priority target-priority chain rather than replacing it. Kill-efficiency (Chapter Approved 2025-26 Bring It Down Fixed secondary: 2 victory points for a destroyed MONSTER/VEHICLE at any wound count, so a low-Wounds War Dog banks the same base 2 victory points as a 26-wound Dominus) drops out of the same kill-fraction formula naturally, per the real-world target-priority doctrine cross-referenced below, rather than needing a separate victory-point-weighted term.

_target_priority_doctrine_reference: https://www.goonhammer.com/start-competing-imperial-knights/ — the same Goonhammer Imperial Knights faction-focus source cited by simulator.focus_fire, which advises committing anti-armour and small arms alike into the models a given weapon profile can actually threaten (the Armigers / War Dogs) rather than washing fire against the Knight's high Toughness and armour save when no matching Anti-keyword or sufficient Strength is present.
